title: Standardizing sales and applying the empirical rule
scenario_markdown: A large sales team's quarterly revenue distribution is approximately bell-shaped, with mean 100 thousand dollars and standard deviation 20 thousand dollars. A representative sells 140 thousand dollars. Use the empirical rule as an approximation, rather than assuming exact normal probabilities.
assumptions: All revenue values use the same units: thousands of dollars.
The empirical rule is appropriate as an approximation for the stated bell-shaped distribution.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is this representative's z-score? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: Subtract the mean before dividing by SD.
The observation is above the mean, so its z-score is positive.

stages.explanation_markdown: $z=(140-100)/20=2$. Excel: `=STANDARDIZE(140,100,20)`. This sales result is two SD above the team mean.

stages.prompt_markdown: Approximately what share of sales results falls from 60 to 140 thousand dollars?

options.text_markdown: About 95%, since these endpoints are two SD below and above the mean.
About 68%, because every symmetric interval contains one SD.
options.hint_markdown: Count how many SD each endpoint is from the mean.

options.text_markdown: Exactly 100%, because no result can be farther than two SD from its mean.
options.hint_markdown: The empirical rule allows observations outside two SD.

stages.explanation_markdown: The interval is $100\pm2(20)$. The empirical rule assigns about 95% of a bell-shaped distribution within two SD. Under an exact normal model the value is about 95.45%, which is a different calculation.

stages.prompt_markdown: Could the same 95% approximation be assumed for a strongly skewed sales distribution?

options.text_markdown: No; mean and SD alone do not justify the bell-shaped empirical-rule percentages.
Yes; every distribution has exactly 95% within two SD.
options.hint_markdown: The empirical rule depends on distribution shape.

options.text_markdown: Yes; positive sales values guarantee symmetry.
options.hint_markdown: Nonnegative support does not imply a bell-shaped distribution.

stages.explanation_markdown: A z-score still standardizes using mean and SD, but empirical-rule percentages require a suitable shape. Check the distribution before using them.
